cleanIntro: ⛔ THERE IS NO FIELD STRIP ON THIS PISTOL, AND THAT IS WALTHER'S CHOICE, NOT A GAP. The LP500 is a pre-charged pneumatic match air pistol: the air lives in a screw-on carbon-aluminium cylinder on the pressure reducer, and pulling the loading gate back opens the loading tray. Walther's maintenance chapter describes exactly one removal, the compressed air cylinder, and tells you to dismantle the pistol only as far as the instructions show. The moving parts carry long-life lubrication that the shooter must not service, and the outside is aluminium and CFRP that must not be oiled. What Walther does publish is short: blow it out, clean the bore from the loading tray toward the muzzle, and grease the cylinder thread about every tenth removal.

steps.title: Safety line, not your eyes — this pistol cannot show you it is empty
steps.action: Before any cleaning, confirm the pistol is not loaded and the barrel is clear. On the LP500 that check is done with the safety line supplied in the case, because there is no way to unload it by hand and nothing on the pistol shows whether a pellet is seated. Hold it firmly, finger away from the trigger, muzzle in a safe direction.
steps.prose: A look into the loading tray is not the check. A pellet already pushed into the barrel is out of sight, and the book is explicit that only the line proves it.
steps.quote: The inspection must be conducted using the safety line because the pistol cannot be unloaded by hand and does not display a loaded status.
steps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 5.2 Conducting a safety inspection, printed p.13
steps.warn: Before shooting or cleaning and in case of malfunction always ensure that the weapon is not loaded and the barrel is free of foreign bodies (see Section 5.2)

steps.title: Loading gate back, line in from the muzzle to the tray
steps.action: Pull the loading gate back until it engages at its rear end position, which opens the loading tray. Push the safety line into the barrel from the muzzle end all the way through to the loading tray, until you see either a pellet or the line itself arrive in the tray. Then take out the pellet or the line, make sure nothing else is in the barrel, and close the loading gate.
steps.prose: The line is a cord, not a rod, and that matters on this barrel: the same book forbids putting a cleaning rod in through the compensator. Walther states the pistol is unloaded and uncocked after the last shot and gives no separate decocking drill in its cleaning chapter, so do not improvise one; if you are unsure of the state, this line check is the book's answer.
steps.aside: Ensure that there are no foreign objects in the barrel.
steps.quote: To inspect, shove the safety line into the barrel opening all the way to the loading tray until you see a pellet or the safety line.
steps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 5.2.1 Inspecting the load status using the safety line, printed p.14

steps.title: Air cylinder off — by hand, no tools, no force
steps.action: Unscrew the compressed air cylinder from the pistol by hand. Walther says it can be unscrewed at any time. Walther's maintenance chapter opens with this removal, and it is the only part the owner takes off for cleaning.
steps.prose: No wrench, strap or pliers: the book bars tools and force on the cylinder both ways, on and off. If it will not turn by hand, stop there rather than reach for something to grip it with.
steps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 8 Maintenance, printed p.39
steps.warn: Do not use force or tools when attaching or removing the compressed air cylinder.

steps.title: ⛔ That is the whole strip — the moving parts are not yours to service
steps.action: Go no further. Walther tells the owner to dismantle the pistol only to the extent its instructions show, and the maintenance chapter shows nothing past the cylinder. The moving parts were lubricated at the factory with long-life lubrication and the book says the shooter must not service them.
steps.prose: Maintenance and service work belong to Walther or a qualified repair shop. A match trigger that has been opened and re-greased by guesswork is a trigger whose feel and weight nobody can vouch for any more.
steps.quote: The movable parts have been treated with long-lasting lubrication and must not be serviced by the shooter.
steps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 8 Maintenance, printed p.39
steps.warn: Only dismantle the weapon to the extent shown in the instructions.

steps.title: Blow the dust and dirt out
steps.action: Blow the pistol out with compressed air to clear dust and dirt. This is the whole outside clean Walther gives.
steps.prose: It replaces the oily rag you would use on a steel gun. On this pistol the rag is the mistake, as the next step says.
steps.quote: The pistol can be blown out with compressed air to free it from dust and dirt.
steps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 8 Maintenance, printed p.39

steps.title: ⛔ No oil or grease on the outside
steps.action: Do not oil or grease the exterior. The pistol is built from aluminium and CFRP, and Walther says those surfaces should not be oiled or greased.
steps.prose: This is the habit from steel guns that does the harm here. Oil on the outside only holds dust and gets carried onto the grip and into the action.
steps.quote: The pistol is made of modern materials like aluminum and CFRP. The exterior should not be oiled or greased.
steps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 8 Maintenance, printed p.39

steps.title: Bore: felt pellets or a pulled patch, tray toward muzzle
steps.action: Clean the inside of the barrel with commercial felt pellets shot through it, or with cleaning patches pulled through on a cleaning line. Either way, clean in the direction the pellet travels: from the loading tray toward the muzzle.
steps.prose: Going with the pellet's path keeps dirt moving out of the muzzle rather than back into the loading tray, where the next pellet seats.
steps.quote: Always clean inside the barrel in the direction of the pellet’s path, in other words, from the loading tray to the barrel.
steps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 8 Maintenance, printed p.39

steps.title: ⛔ Never a cleaning rod through the compensator
steps.action: Do not push a cleaning rod into the barrel from the compensator end. Patches go on a cleaning line, and felt pellets go in at the loading tray.
steps.prose: The rule is absolute in the book and it fits the direction rule above: nothing goes into this barrel from the muzzle end except the safety line, which is a cord.
steps.quote: Never insert a cleaning rod into the barrel through the compensator.
steps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 8 Maintenance, printed p.39

steps.title: Field clean complete: cylinder back on by hand, then a safety inspection
steps.action: Screw the compressed air cylinder back onto the pistol by hand until it is tight, with no tool. Check the pressure on its built-in gauge. Then run the safety line check again before you shoot: Walther calls for a safety inspection after the cylinder is attached.
steps.prose: Hand-tight is the instruction. A tool on the cylinder is barred in both directions, and putting the cylinder on does not end the job until the line has been through the bore.
steps.quote: screw the compressed air cylinder onto the pistol by hand until tight.
steps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 7.2 Filling the compressed air cylinder, printed p.38

deepSteps.title: About every tenth removal: silicone grease on the thread
deepSteps.action: After roughly the tenth time the cylinder has been taken off and put back, lightly grease the thread on the connection pieces of the pressure reducer with an acid-free silicone grease. Walther calls this the one exception to its no-lubrication rule.
deepSteps.prose: Light is the word, and acid-free silicone grease is the only lubricant this book lets the owner put anywhere on the pistol. The thread only needs enough to keep the cylinder turning on by hand.
deepSteps.quote: As an exception, after about the tenth removal and reattachment of the compressed air cylinder, lightly lubricate the thread on the connection pieces of the pressure reducer with an acid-free silicon grease.
deepSteps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 8 Maintenance, printed p.39

deepSteps.title: Laying it up for weeks: cylinder off to save the seals
deepSteps.action: In regular use the cylinder can stay on. If the pistol is going to sit unused for several weeks, unscrew the compressed air cylinder so the seals are not held under pressure. Store the pistol unloaded and uncocked, in its case, in a dry room at room temperature.
deepSteps.prose: This is the step people skip, and the seals are what it protects. A seal left under pressure for weeks is a seal that leaks later.
deepSteps.quote: If you do not intend to use the pistol for several weeks, unscrew the compressed air cylinder to preserve the seals
deepSteps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 5.3.4 Storing the pistol, printed p.15

deepSteps.title: Inspect the cylinder every time, and know its age
deepSteps.action: Look the cylinder over for tears or damage before every use. Its maximum service life is 10 years. A CFRP cylinder may be retested by the manufacturer once for a further 10 years, and the permissible service life is shown on the cylinder itself. Keep it between −20 °C and +50 °C, never fill past 200 bar, and never mark, scratch or engrave it.
deepSteps.prose: The cylinder is the part of this pistol with a hard expiry date, and the date is printed on it. Read it at every clean.
deepSteps.quote: Inspect the compressed air cylinder for tears or damage before each use.
deepSteps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 7.1 Safety instructions for handling compressed air cylinders, printed p.37
deepSteps.warn: The compressed air cylinder has a maximum service life of 10 years.

deepSteps.title: ⛔ A leaking, damaged or expired cylinder: empty it, never refill it
deepSteps.action: Do not refill a cylinder that leaks or is otherwise unsafe; empty it safely. To empty it, unscrew it from the pistol and slowly screw the supplied filling adapter onto it; the air drains out audibly until the cylinder is completely empty. Wear hearing protection and make anyone nearby wear it too. Only the manufacturer may repair the cylinder.
deepSteps.prose: The noise is the point of the warning: 200 bar leaving through an adapter is loud enough to damage hearing. An emptied cylinder is also the only kind that may go by air or by post.
deepSteps.quote: Do not refill leaky and/or otherwise unsafe compressed air cylinders. Please empty safely.
deepSteps.cite: LP500 MATCH AIR PISTOL — LP500 cal. .177 (4.5mm) — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS — 2833549.CW.02-18.0,2.21 rev.b (print code on the last page of each language run — February 2018); the maker's download file name reads Rev_d, the printed code is what is quoted — 7.1 Safety instructions for handling compressed air cylinders, printed p.37
deepSteps.warn: Always wear hearing protection when emptying compressed air cylinders.

cleaning.name: CLEAR
tasks: Safety line through the bore to the loading tray — the pistol cannot show its load state

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE
tasks: ⛔ No oil or grease on the aluminium and CFRP exterior

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Felt pellets shot through, or patches pulled through on a cleaning line
Loading tray toward the muzzle — the pellet's direction
⛔ Never a cleaning rod in through the compensator

cleaning.name: AIR CYLINDER
tasks: Off and on by hand only, never with a tool or force
Pressure-reducer thread lightly greased with acid-free silicone grease about every tenth removal
Inspected for tears or damage before each use; service life on the cylinder

cleaning.name: NEVER
tasks: Servicing the moving parts — factory long-life lubrication
Dismantling past what the instructions show

reassembly: Cylinder thread checked; acid-free silicone grease if it is about the tenth removal.
Cylinder screwed onto the pistol by hand until tight — no tool, no force.
Pressure read on the cylinder's built-in gauge.
Safety inspection with the safety line before shooting.
fncheck: With the cylinder back on hand-tight, read its built-in pressure gauge, and fill it if necessary before shooting. Then run the safety inspection again: pull the loading gate back until it engages, push the safety line from the muzzle through to the loading tray, take the line out, make sure the barrel is clear, and close the gate. Walther calls for that inspection after filling and attaching the cylinder ("Conduct a safety inspection after filling and attaching the compressed air cylinder (see Section 5.2).", printed p.13). ⛔ If the cylinder will not seat by hand, do not force it or put a tool on it.
